content.text:
I built the deliverable, `/work/spec.vl.json`, and it renders with no errors or warnings. In the rendered image, the overview shows all five years and the detail panels show a pre-selected week, 8–15 July 2024, down to single 10-minute readings. I did not test dragging the brush interactively. Dragging should be slow when the selection covers several years, because the detail view then draws up to about 263,000 points.

- **Overview:** daily mean temperature as a line, with the daily minimum–maximum as a shaded band. These daily values are computed inside the spec from all rows. You drag on it to choose the detail period.
- **Detail, temperature:** every 10-minute temperature reading as a line with a point at each reading.
- **Detail, precipitation:** a separate bar track below, sharing the same time axis.

```
REPORT
deliverable: spec.vl.json
requirements:
  R1: done - daily mean line + daily min–max band of tl, 2020–2024, aggregated in-spec
  R2: done - detail line+points at every 10-min reading inside the brushed range
  R3: done - interval brush on overview sets x-domain and filter of both detail tracks
  R4: done - separate rr track (mm per 10 min) below tl, same brushed UTC x-domain
  R5: done - overview "%b %Y" labels; detail uses automatic UTC multi-format (days → hours → minutes)
  R6: done - full CSV loaded from URL; aggregation only in the overview transform
  R7: done - axes in °C, mm per 10 min, UTC; title + one-sentence caption (subtitle)
assumptions:
  - Time stamp marks the end of the 10-min interval; rr bars span [time−10 min, time]
  - The initial brush (8–15 Jul 2024) is a view choice, not a data value; the reader can move it
  - Overview uses daily aggregation (mean, min, max) to keep the 5-year view readable
  - Caption describes the visible qualitative pattern (annual cycle, diurnal swing, short rain bursts) without numbers
limitations:
  - Brushing a multi-year range in the detail view draws up to ~263k points and is slow
  - Only intervals with rr > 0 are drawn as bars; zero-rain intervals are blank
  - Empty fields (missing values) are skipped in the aggregates and are not flagged visually
```
